title: Surfaces, Gutters, Insets, Pending & Staging
description: Five patterns that work the space around the content: shader surfaces, rules in the gaps, underline insets, pending snap targets and a staging tray.

drops.title: Shader Surfaces
drops.description: Three cards whose background is a live fragment shader — domain-warped fbm, a specular fold and pointer-pulled flow.
drops.concept: Shader-backed component libraries were the breakout UI repo of late 2026: instead of a frozen gradient, the card's surface is a WebGL program that keeps moving. This drop runs one fragment shader across three canvases with different colour uniforms, warps the noise domain by its own fbm, and lets the pointer drag the field. Speed, scale, warp and grain are live uniforms; without WebGL each card falls back to an animated CSS gradient.
drops.source: MengTo/threeui — shader-backed UI component catalog (6k stars in its first month)

interaction.mouse: Move over a card and the flow leans toward the pointer.
interaction.click: Drag the uniform sliders to re-tune every surface at once.
interaction.touch: Touch-drag across a card does the same as hover.

drops.title: Rules In The Gaps
drops.description: column-rule escapes multicol, row-rule joins it, and a bento grid finally paints its own gutters.
drops.concept: CSS Gap Decorations shipped in Chromium in June 2026 and generalise the old multicol column-rule to grid and flex, adding row-rule alongside it. Because the lines are painted rather than laid out, adding them never shifts a tile — and rule-inset-junction decides how the crossings breathe. Shown on a spanning bento grid, a wrapping flex rail and the multicol layout it came from; where the browser lacks support the same gutters are measured and drawn so the pattern still reads.
drops.source: utilitybend — “CSS is filling the gaps with rules”

interaction.mouse: Slide rule width and junction inset; pick a colour pair.
interaction.click: Swatches restyle every gutter on the page at once.
interaction.touch: Layout reflows to two columns; the rules follow the new gutters.

drops.title: Underlines With Padding
drops.description: text-decoration-inset trims a rule back to the glyphs, or pushes it out into an editorial bracket — and animates between the two.
drops.concept: Underlines have always overshot the first and last character, which is why designers rebuilt them out of pseudo-elements. text-decoration-inset (Chrome 154) gives the decoration a start and end inset: positive values pull it in, negative values outset it past the text run, and the property is animatable, so hover can wipe a rule into place. Four specimens cover trimming, outsetting, the hover wipe and the neighbouring text-decoration-skip-spaces.
drops.source: CSS-Tricks — “text-decoration-inset is Like Padding for Text Decorations”

interaction.mouse: Hover a link in specimen 03 to wipe its underline in.
interaction.click: Drag start/end/thickness/offset and read the generated declaration.
interaction.touch: Tap a link to trigger the same wipe; the panel hides on small screens.

drops.title: Pending Snap
drops.description: The snap target lights up mid-gesture via scrollsnapchanging, and commits on scrollsnapchange.
drops.concept: A scroll-snap container knows which item it would rest on long before the gesture ends. scrollsnapchanging hands you that pending target so the UI can lean into it early — the classic trick behind native-feeling pickers — while scrollsnapchange confirms the landing. A cover rail, a date strip and a two-column wheel picker all report both events, and each rail keeps its cross axis unscrollable with the single-axis overflow: auto clip that landed in Chrome 153.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers — single-axis scroll containers (Chrome 153) and scroll snap events

interaction.mouse: Drag or wheel a rail — the pending card glows blue before it commits in amber.
interaction.click: Click any card, chip or wheel row to scroll it to centre.
interaction.touch: Flick each rail; the readouts and event log update per gesture.

drops.title: Staged Uploads
drops.description: The file input rethought as an editable staging tray: per-row state machines, retries in place and an undoable remove.
drops.concept: Upload controls usually fire the moment a file is chosen. A staging tray keeps the queue editable instead: files land as rows you can reorder in your head, start individually or all at once, pause, retry a failure and remove — with a snackbar that can put the row back. Every row owns its own queued → uploading → done / failed machine and renders its own progress; nothing leaves the page, the transfer is simulated locally.

interaction.mouse: Drop files on the zone, or use Add samples; hit play/stop/retry per row.
interaction.click: Upload all staggers every row; Clear finished sweeps the done ones.
interaction.touch: Tap the drop zone to browse; the tray and snackbar are thumb-sized.
